title: Essential-image test on derived maps into simplicial categories
statement:
Use simplicial categories and the Bergner homotopy category $h\mathrm{sCat}$ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. For a simplicial category $T$, let $\pi_0T$ have the objects of $T$ and the connected components of its mapping simplicial sets as morphisms. Let $j:T\to T'$ be a simplicial functor inducing a weak homotopy equivalence $T(x,y)\to T'(jx,jy)$ for every pair of objects. For every small simplicial category $I$, postcomposition is injective:
$$j_*:\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,T)\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathrm{sCat}}(I,T').$$
Its image consists exactly of the classes $a$ for which the induced functor $\pi_0I\to\pi_0T'$, defined up to natural isomorphism, has essential image contained in that of $\pi_0j$. Essential image means objects isomorphic to an object in the image. All categories and hom sets fit in a fixed sufficiently large universe. No essential-surjectivity hypothesis on $j$ is assumed.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11, printed p.889; maps in the Bergner homotopy category are tested on their induced ordinary homotopy-category functor. Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial homotopy-theoretic result.

proof.text: Use the functorial object-preserving replacements T→RT and T′→RT′ of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Naturality gives the commuting square of mapping simplicial sets with horizontal maps T(x,y)→T′(jx,jy) and RT(x,y)→RT′(jx,jy). The vertical maps and the top map are weak homotopy equivalences, so two-out-of-three makes the bottom map a weak homotopy equivalence. Put X=N_hc(RT), Y=N_hc(RT′), and J=N_hc(Rj). The natural mapping-space comparisons in that node identify the bottom map with Map_X(x,y)→Map_Y(Jx,Jy). Thus J is fully faithful. Put A=N_hc(RI); no cofibrancy assumption on I is needed.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11 and the mapping-space comparison preceding it, printed p.889.

proof.text: Let Y₀ be the full subcategory of Y on the objects equivalent to Jx for some x∈X, and let i:Y₀→Y be the inclusion. By [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], J factors as iJ₀ and J₀:X→Y₀ admits a coherent quasi-inverse K:Y₀→X, with coherent natural equivalences KJ₀≃1_X and J₀K≃1_Y₀. Its hypotheses hold because Step 1 proves full faithfulness and Y₀ is exactly the full replete essential image specified in that node.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1, applied by the existing full-essential-image node.

proof.text: The derived coherent-nerve equivalence in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identifies Hom_{h sCat}(I,T) with coherent functors A→X modulo coherent natural equivalence, and identifies Hom_{h sCat}(I,T′) with coherent functors A→Y modulo coherent natural equivalence. These are the morphisms in the ordinary homotopy category of Cat_∞. Naturality identifies j_* with postcomposition by J. All objects and functor categories are taken in the sufficiently large universe of the statement. It therefore remains to check injectivity and the image criterion for these functors.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11 and the Bergner-to-Joyal comparison, printed p.889.

proof.text: By [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], a full subcategory contains precisely all simplices with its specified vertices. Thus a simplicial map a:A→Y whose vertices lie in Y₀ factors literally as ia₀ with a₀:A→Y₀. Moreover an equivalence between iJ₀F and iJ₀G in Fun(A,Y) factors into Fun(A,Y₀): its transformation, its inverse, and the two inverse-triangle witnesses have all vertices among the values of J₀F and J₀G. (For a chain of such equivalences the same argument applies, since Y₀ is replete.) Applying K and whiskering KJ₀≃1_X from Step 2 yields F≃KJ₀F≃KJ₀G≃G, proving injectivity. For a functor a=ia₀ as above, put b=Ka₀. Whiskering J₀K≃1_Y₀ gives Jb=iJ₀Ka₀≃ia₀=a. Conversely every Jb has all vertices in Y₀. This proves that the image consists precisely of functors whose vertex values lie in Y₀, without choosing separate, potentially incompatible lifts of their arrows.

source.place: Corollary A.3.4.11, printed p.889, essential-image assertion; explicit full-subcategory argument in the coherent-nerve model, rather than the printed chunk proof.

proof.text: The object-preserving replacement and mapping-space comparison in [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison] identify π₀T with the ordinary homotopy category of X, and π₀T′ with that of Y, naturally for j; the same applies to I and A. Composition agrees because the comparison preserves enriched composition. An object y of Y lies in Y₀ exactly when y and Jx are isomorphic in its homotopy category for some x. Here the homotopy category of the quasicategory Y has as morphisms the components of the right-pinched mapping spaces Map_Y(y,y′) of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], that is, homotopy classes of edges, and a 2-simplex with edges f:y→y′, g:y′→y″ and long edge h says [h]=[g][f]. If f:y→Jx is an equivalence in the sense of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], its inverse g and the two triangle witnesses (2-simplices with edges (f,g,1_y) and (g,f,1_{Jx})) give [g][f]=[1_y] and [f][g]=[1_{Jx}]. Conversely let [f],[g] be inverse classes. Fill the inner horn Λ²₁ given by (f,g) to a 2-simplex σ with long edge h. Then [h]=[1_y], so h and 1_y lie in one component of the Kan complex Map_Y(y,y) and are joined by an edge (in either direction, the space being Kan). Such an edge is a homotopy between h and 1_y, and by the equivalence of the two forms of homotopy (Scholze, basic fact (2)) it gives a 2-simplex τ with edges h, 1_y and long edge 1_y. The inner horn Λ³₂ on vertices y,Jx,y,y with faces d₃=σ, d₁=τ and d₀ the degenerate 2-simplex on g fills in Y, and its face d₂ is a 2-simplex with edges (f,g,1_y). The other witness is obtained in the same way from [f][g]=[1_{Jx}]. This is Scholze's basic fact (3) of Lecture II. Thus the vertex condition of Step 4 is exactly the stated essential-image condition on π₀a. Equivalent coherent functors induce naturally isomorphic homotopy-category functors, by taking the components and naturality triangles of the coherent equivalence; hence this condition is independent of the representative of a. Combining Steps 3-4 proves both clauses, without essential surjectivity of j.
